newsitem.title: USA: CME LIVE CATTLE SEEN STEADY TO UP, FEEDERS LOWER.
newsitem.headline: CME LIVE CATTLE SEEN STEADY TO UP, FEEDERS LOWER.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb higher while feeder cattle were called 0.250 to 0.500 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Talk that packer interest for fed cattle has increased Tuesday morning should encourage demand for live cattle futures. Packers are short of slaughter ready supplies and bottoming action in the boxed beef market may also provide support, analysts said.
Deferred months may also show further support on expectations of tighter fed supplies later, they said.

Some estimates on Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report pointed to placements starting to fall below year-ago levels. Early July placement estimates for the major seven states were ranging from 96 to 105 percent of a year ago. On-feed estimates thus far were estimated between 115 to 117 percent and marketings 103 to 107 percent of a year ago.

Feeder cattle were expected to be pressured from the start following Tuesday morning's USDA crop production estimates for corn which at 9.276 billion bushels, indicated less corn than most market watchers expected.
Concern over feed costs have weighed on feeders recently with a declining CME feeder cattle index adding to pressure, analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.25 at $81.28 per cwt.
